_why: The assembler exists to make five recorded hand-assembly mistakes unrepeatable, so each of those has a mutation restoring it. The rest defend the two things that are judgement rather than default -- the stated counts and the wiring pin -- and the task slicer, where truncating or over-running a task body ships the wrong scope with no visible error. Every mutation is born pinned to the one test it is aimed at.

mutations.name: default-the-missing-counts
mutations._mechanism: The judgement the row explicitly carves out. A default decides whether an immediate pass is a guard or a weakened test.
mutations.find: elif phase == "red" and (expect_fail is None or expect_pass is None):

mutations.name: treat-zero-counts-as-absent
mutations._mechanism: `--expect-pass 0` is a real answer. A falsy test would refuse a correct dispatch and read as strictness.
mutations.find: elif phase == "red" and (expect_fail is None or expect_pass is None):
mutations.replace: elif phase == "red" and (not expect_fail or not expect_pass):

mutations.name: drop-the-model-pin
mutations._mechanism: Mistake 1. The config default cannot execute tools and fails as a well-formed STATUS: BLOCKED, so nothing downstream looks wrong.

mutations.name: skip-the-interpreter-probe
mutations._mechanism: Mistake 2. A bare python3 is 3.14 here and the independent re-run errors instead of measuring.

mutations.name: probe-always-passes
mutations._mechanism: A detector that cannot fail makes every interpreter refusal vacuous -- the accept direction of the same guard.

mutations.name: allow-the-read-only-sandbox
mutations._mechanism: Mistake 4. Kills pytest's tempdir, so the run passes without measuring anything.

mutations.name: drop-the-scope-warning
mutations._mechanism: Mistake 5. Without it the agent widens the run and collects the sibling project.
mutations.find: "That path is the scope. Do not widen it — an unscoped run collects the "

mutations.name: stop-the-task-body-at-any-heading
mutations._mechanism: A task whose body has its own sub-heading would be truncated at the first one, silently shipping half a task.
mutations.find: starts = [i for i, ln in enumerate(lines) if _TASK_RE.match(ln)]
mutations.replace: starts = [i for i, ln in enumerate(lines) if ln.startswith("#")]

mutations.name: let-the-task-body-run-past-the-next-task
mutations._mechanism: The dispatch would carry the following tasks too, so the agent implements out of scope.
mutations.find: end = starts[position + 1] if position + 1 < len(starts) else len(lines)

mutations.name: accept-a-wiring-task-with-no-pin
mutations._mechanism: Nothing downstream can see the wire; 5e would establish GREEN for a connection with no load-bearing test.
mutations.find:
if not meta["pin"]:
            raise Halt("no_wire_pin", f"task={task_id}")

mutations.name: gate-a-wiring-task-on-counts
mutations._mechanism: Counts cannot gate a wiring task -- the RED split returns identically whether or not the wire exists.

mutations.name: drop-the-residual-slot-preflight
mutations._mechanism: A raw <INLINE_...> reaching the agent reads as an unfilled template and is silently discounted.

mutations.name: preflight-matches-bare-prose-slot-names
mutations._mechanism: Prose names a slot bare; only a real slot is bracketed. Matching bare names refuses every assembly against the shipped template.

mutations.name: emit-the-same-phase-directive-for-both
mutations._mechanism: The template carries BOTH RED and GREEN instructions; without the stamp the agent picks.
mutations.find: "green": "**THIS DISPATCH IS PHASE 5e (GREEN).** Make the failing tests "
mutations.replace: "green": "**THIS DISPATCH IS PHASE 5d (RED).** Make the failing tests "

_why_not_write_before_halt: A `write-the-prompt-before-the-halt` mutation was written and REMOVED as equivalent, recorded here so a later reader does not re-add it. In `main()` the prompt write sits after the `except Halt: return 2`, and `filled` does not exist before `assemble()` returns -- so a halt structurally cannot reach the write and there is no mutant that makes it. The property 'a halt writes no prompt' is guaranteed by order, not by a guard, and TestCli::test_a_halt_exits_two_and_writes_no_prompt asserts it directly. An equivalent mutant reports as `survived`, which is byte-identical to a real coverage gap.
